scope: Sequential within-patient synthetic-resolution diagnostic, specified before its new outcomes. Addresses scanner/site confounding in the previous observational spacing groups.
patients: All patients with native z spacing <=2.5 mm in the original40 and prior fresh20 cohorts; no new replication40 patients included
models: Existing frozen continuation 40k development-selected checkpoints; no retraining
preprocessing: Native-z Gaussian sigma=.5*sqrt((target/native_spacing)^2-1), truncate 3, nearest boundary. Linear sampling onto a coarse grid with the target physical spacing, phase aligned to native origin; extend last retained plane; identical common 3-mm resampling and HU normalization. Fractional sampling ratios require linear interpolation on the coarse grid.
controls: On every prior 5-mm native-spacing patient, target=15 mm must reproduce the existing f3 float16 input exactly. Retain the central image condition equally for repeated and contextual models. Native labels unchanged.
contrast: Within the same thin-acquisition patients, compare context-by-augmentation at target15 minus target6; also show all four model losses and context gains at both targets
metrics: Native-grid patient macro Dice and HD95; common 9-mm scan-interior Dice sensitivity analysis
statistics: Average three seed-specific patient metrics; 10000 paired patient bootstrap, seed 2026111506; all intervals exploratory, unadjusted. Patient-matched intervention holds patient/scanner fixed but does not reproduce all real acquisition changes.
interpretation: Tests whether more severe absolute through-plane information loss can change context/augmentation behavior within the same cases. It cannot establish that native scanner spacing alone explains the prior between-group association.
